overview.description: 6-Card Brag is a complex partition and vying game that bridges the gap between standard Brag and 9-Card Brag. Every player is dealt six cards and must divide them into two independent three-card hands. These hands are typically played against opponents in sequence (front and back) or used to decide a single highest-rank winner. It rewards both the skill of hand optimization and the traditional bluffing and blind-betting mechanics of the Brag family.

history.origins: Developed as a strategic expansion of British pub Brag, 6-Card Brag introduces the 'partition' mechanic found in Asian games like Chinese Poker but retains the core British vying structure.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Partition variants of Brag appear in Northern English card rooms.
1980s: Standardized as a specialty 'big hand' variant.
Present: Played in competitive Brag circles and high-stakes social games.
history.evolution: The transition from a single three-card hand to two simultaneous hands forced a total recalibration of betting strategies, as a player might have one unbeatable hand and one complete bluff.
history.cultural: Regarded as a 'thinking man's' Brag, where the math of partitioning cards is as vital as the bluffing.

setup.equipment: Standard pack, betting chips or currency.
setup.dealing: Ante into pot. Deal six cards face-down to each player. Players divide their six cards into two separate three-card hands.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest-ranked hands across the partition or by forcing others to fold.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Partition**: Players divide 6 cards into Hand A and Hand B. 2. **Vying**: Betting rounds proceed as in standard Brag. 3. **Comparison**: Showdown involves comparing corresponding hands. 4. **Ranks**: Prial > Running Flush > Run > Flush > Pair > High Card.
keyRules: Both three-card hands must be legal Brag combinations.
In many variants, you must win both hand comparisons to take the entire pot; otherwise, it carries over.
Blind betting applies to the entire 6-card set before viewing and partitioning.

strategy.basic: Avoid making one 'Super Hand' and one 'Trash Hand'. A balanced partition (e.g., two Flushes) is often more reliable than a single Prial and a High-Card hand.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Front' Signal: If playing in rounds, winning the first hand comparison puts immense pressure on the opponent. Invest your best cards in Hand A if you intend to bluff Hand B.
strategy.advanced: Range Splitting: Evaluate the total number of trumps and high cards in the 6-card deal. If the deck is 'heavy' with Spades, splitting your Spades across two hands might be a safer defensive move than one strong Flush.
tips: Don't ignore the High Card tie-breakers; kickers are vital in partition games.
If you are dealt four of a kind, you have two pairs or a Prial—choose the split that maximizes your win probability across both comparisons.

list.name: 9-Card Brag
list.description: Partitioning nine cards into three hands; the final evolution of the multi-card Brag series.
list.emptyOverridesReason: No engine overrides; referenced variation shares core Brag structure.

difficulty.easy: Partitions hands randomly. Sees cards immediately. Only bets on Prials.
difficulty.medium: Uses a greedy algorithm to form the highest possible single hand. Understands basic pot odds.
difficulty.hard: Optimizes the partition for maximum win-probability across both hands (Minimax). Tracks opponent betting 'tells' during the partition phase.

considerations: Requires a combinatorial solver for 6-choose-3-choose-3 hand optimization.
Betting engine must handle multi-hand showdown resolution.

additional: Traditional British Card Games (Oxford University Press)

ante.description: Contribute a fixed amount to the pot before the deal.
ante.constraints: Allowed only during the ante phase.

deal.reason: The distribution of six cards face-down to all players is handled by the system dealer.

reveal_market.reason: 6-Card Brag is a hole-card game where all cards are held privately; no community market exists.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase cards from a market; hand optimization is restricted to the initial partition.

buy_stock.reason: There is no drawing or buying from the stock during play; the round uses the six cards dealt at the start.

fold.description: Abandon the hand and forfeit all chips in the pot.
fold.constraints: Allowed during the vying phase when facing a bet.

check.reason: Standard Brag requires an active bet to remain in the hand; checking is generally not permitted.

call.description: Match the current bet level (price depends on whether player is Blind or Seeing).
call.constraints: Allowed only during the vying phase.

bet.description: Place or increase a wager into the pot.
bet.constraints: Seeing players must bet at least double the Blind bet amount.

raise.description: Increase the size of the current bet.

declare.reason: Hand results are established during the showdown comparison rather than through a separate declaration.

reveal_hand.reason: The system automatically reveals partitions at the request of a player who pays the 'See' double-cost.

award_pot.description: Distribute the pot to the winner at showdown or the last player standing.

play_card.reason: 6-Card Brag is a partition vying game where cards are held rather than played to tricks.

draw.reason: All six cards are received at the start; no drawing phase exists during the play of the hand.

discard.reason: Every card must be partitioned into the two hands; no cards are discarded to a muck pile.

pass.reason: Players must either bet, see, or fold during their turn; a simple pass is not supported.

bid.reason: Brag uses a wagering system rather than an auction-style bidding system for contracts.

meld.reason: Hand resolution is based strictly on three-card poker hierarchies rather than forming melds.

go_out.reason: The hand terminates only after a showdown occurs or all but one player have folded.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: Standard 6-card Brag does not include a draw pile or exchange mechanic after the initial partition.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: All cards are partitioned into two hands; no discarding or mucking is allowed.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Cards contribute only their rank and suit values to hand combinations; no individual card has a secondary effect.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: Wagering results are immediate and public; no hidden tokens are required.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: 6-Card Brag is a partition/vying game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: This game is not a shedding game; players maintain their hands throughout the deal.

customActions.description: Distribute six cards face-down to each player at the start of the round.
Divide the six dealt cards into two separate three-card Brag hands.
Bet on the hand without looking at the chosen three cards.
Pay double price to see the cards before betting.
Bet on the hand after paying to see the cards.
Request a showdown to determine the winner between remaining players.
Compare the two three-card partition hands according to Brag hierarchy rules.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; specialized Brag hierarchy determines the winning hands at showdown.
engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for six-card Brag where prials, runs, and flushes are ranked and ace may be high or low in runs.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Flushes (six of the same suit) and running flushes (six consecutive ranks in the same suit) are ranked hands. Suits do not break ties between equal hand types in Brag.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit; for prials the three is the highest rank, then two, ace, king down to four. For runs, ace may be high or low. Standard Brag order: prial of threes best, then runs, then flushes, then pairs, then high card.

hero.title: 6-CARD BRAG
hero.subtitle: The Double Hand Duel
hero.tagline: One deal. Two hands. Twice the bluffing.

synthesis.shortDescription: A sophisticated partition variant of Brag. Every player receives six cards and must divide them into two independent three-card hands. Win both hand comparisons to sweep the pot, or use one strong hand to bluff through a weak second. Strategic division is as vital as the bet.

prompts.human: You have a pair of 3s, an Ace of Hearts, a 2 of Hearts, a 3 of Hearts, and a King. Do you put the 3s together for a winning pair, or split your cards to make a Flush in Hearts and a high-card King hand?
prompts.ai: Game: 6-Card Brag. Type: Partition/Vying. Rules: 6 cards dealt, split into 2 hands of 3. Brag rankings apply. Vying follows standard blind/see costs. Win both comparisons to claim pot.

scoring.description: Standard pot-based resolution across dual-hand comparisons.
scoring.winCondition: Win both hand comparisons OR be the last player not to fold.

penalties.Split Win: If hand comparisons result in a split between two players, the pot carries over to the next round.

scoring.splitRules: Pot carried over if no single player wins both hand matchups.

nullReasons.targetScore: No fixed target score; play until the session concludes.
nullReasons.cardValues: Individual cards determine hand rankings rather than having point values.
